title: Workspace Outbound Access Protection (OAP) for Real-Time Intelligence
summary: Microsoft rounds up Workspace Outbound Access Protection (preview) support across the full Real-Time Intelligence surface — Eventstream, Eventhouse, KQL Queryset, Real-Time Dashboard, and Activator — detailing per-item which outbound scenarios remain supported under a default-deny policy and which are currently blocked, including a recurring Copilot-related restriction.
audience: Fabric security admins and RTI architects deciding whether to enable workspace-level outbound network controls on real-time ingestion, analytics, dashboarding, and automation workloads without breaking existing pipelines.
why_it_matters: Real-Time Intelligence spans several distinct item types with different outbound needs (streaming ingestion, KQL storage/query, dashboards, automated actions), so a single OAP toggle affects each differently; this post is the item-by-item reference admins need to predict what breaks and what to explicitly allow before turning OAP on in a workspace already running RTI workloads.
takeaways: OAP for RTI is in preview and covers Eventstream, Eventhouse, KQL Queryset, Real-Time Dashboard, and Activator, though not every end-to-end scenario is enabled yet.

Eventhouse under OAP keeps Azure Event Hubs ingestion and same-workspace OneLake/Eventstream/follower-database access, but blocks non-Event-Hubs external connections and Copilot-powered query/analysis.
KQL Queryset is minimally affected by OAP because it mainly queries data already inside Fabric; the main restriction is Copilot-assisted query authoring.
Real-Time Dashboard keeps its core viewing/monitoring experience under OAP; Copilot-assisted tile editing/exploration and editor-identity-based sharing are blocked.

Activator's OAP behavior varies by destination: same-workspace Fabric item targets are always allowed, Teams notifications are tenant-restricted and configurable, email is blocked by default to same-tenant recipients, and Power Automate triggers are blocked outright with no current override.

claims.text: Eventhouse now supports Workspace Outbound Access Protection in preview; when enabled, Eventhouse keeps working with Azure Event Hubs ingestion plus same-workspace Eventstream, OneLake, and follower-database access, while direct access to Eventhouse databases outside supported OneLake shortcut paths and connections to non-Event-Hubs external resources are blocked.

Under Eventhouse OAP, OneLake and follower-database access to other Fabric workspaces is possible but only when the workspace admin configures the appropriate data connection access rules, rather than being allowed by default.

Copilot-powered query generation and data analysis features for Eventhouse are not supported when workspace OAP is enabled, a restriction the post calls intentional to keep outbound access tightly governed in protected workspaces.

KQL Queryset now supports OAP; because KQL Queryset primarily queries data already available inside Fabric rather than reaching external destinations, standard query authoring and interactive data exploration continue to work unchanged under a default-deny outbound policy.

The primary restriction for KQL Queryset under OAP in this preview is that Copilot-powered KQL query generation is not supported, while manually authored queries and existing investigation workflows are unaffected.

Real-Time Dashboard now supports OAP; most day-to-day dashboard viewing and monitoring of operational metrics continues to work unchanged, since the outbound access model for RTD is described as intentionally simple.

Under Workspace OAP, Real-Time Dashboard blocks Copilot-assisted tile add/edit, Copilot-assisted real-time data exploration, and sharing a dashboard using the dashboard editor's own identity, while standard outbound access scenarios remain supported.

Activator now supports Workspace OAP; actions targeting Fabric items (notebooks, Spark jobs, pipelines, User Data Functions, Dataflows) in the same workspace are always allowed, while actions targeting items in other workspaces are blocked unless the workspace admin explicitly permits them via data connection rules.

Under Activator OAP, Microsoft Teams notifications are restricted to the same tenant and are configurable per workspace via a Teams connection kind in data connection rules; email notifications are blocked by default and limited to same-tenant recipients; Power Automate flows triggered from Activator are blocked outright and cannot currently be re-enabled through data connection rules.

Eventstream's OAP behavior (covered more fully in a companion post on Fabric/Azure event flows) continues to allow routing events to Real-Time Intelligence and other Fabric items within the same workspace, while cross-workspace destinations and external service/database/API destinations are blocked by default.
